headline: Obama was sworn in on January 20, Michael Jackson died in June, and unemployment reached 10 percent in October
texture: Circuit City announced on January 16 that all 567 of its American stores would close and 34,000 jobs with them, after nearly sixty years in business. A Federal Reserve report on March 13 said American families had lost 18 percent of their wealth in the previous year. The Chicago Cubs filed for Chapter 11 protection on October 12. The small business lender CIT Group filed on November 1, which likely cancelled its obligation to repay a $2.3 billion loan from the Troubled Asset Relief Program.

At 23:31:30 UTC on February 13, the decimal representation of Unix time reached 1234567890. Bushfires in Victoria on February 7 killed 173 people in what the world year page calls the worst natural disaster in Australia's history. Iceland's government and banking system collapsed on January 26 and Geir Haarde resigned the same day. Johanna Sigurdardottir replaced him on February 1 as the world's first openly lesbian head of government. Greenland gained self-rule on June 21, and Slovakia had swapped the koruna for the euro on January 1.

Obama signed executive orders on January 22 to close the Guantanamo Bay detention camp inside a year and to prohibit torture in terrorism interrogations. Arlen Specter left the Republicans on April 28, and Al Franken was seated on July 7 after an eight-month recount, which took the Democrats to sixty Senate seats. Navy snipers killed three Somali pirates on April 12 to free the captain of the Maersk Alabama, hijacked four days earlier. The first 9/12 Project rally drew somewhere between hundreds of thousands and two million people to Washington on September 12.

A cloned Pyrenean Ibex was born alive in January, the first animal from an extinct species brought back that way, and died seven minutes later from defects in its lungs. Paleontologists pulled 28 fossils of the giant snake T. cerrejonensis out of coal mines at Cerrejon in Colombia on February 5. New York opened two ballparks in the same spring, the new Yankee Stadium and Citi Field, and Mark Buehrle of the Chicago White Sox threw the 18th perfect game in major league history.

pol.us_president.label: US President
pol.us_president.detail: The 44th president and the first African American to hold the office. Joe Biden became the 47th vice president the same day, and George W. Bush's second term ended that morning. John Roberts remained Chief Justice.

pol.inauguration.label: First inauguration of Barack Obama
pol.inauguration.value: The 56th presidential inauguration, on the West Front of the United States Capitol
pol.inauguration.detail: January 20 is the date fixed for an inauguration, and both cached year pages give it, so there is no disagreement to name. Roberts and Obama both misplaced words in the oath, and the White House counsel asked the Chief Justice to administer it again as a precaution, which he did on the evening of January 21 in the Map Room of the White House. Organisers opened the whole length of the National Mall as a viewing area, and the inauguration's own article says the event set a record attendance for anything held in the city.

pol.us_congress.label: US Congress
pol.us_congress.detail: The US year page puts the start of the term on January 3 and the convening on January 6, when Democrats held 256 seats in the House and 59 in the Senate. Obama gave his first address to it on February 24, defending the bank bailouts as necessary and warning that more might be needed. Members spent the August 3 to September 4 recess on town halls about health care in their districts.

pol.stimulus.label: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act
pol.stimulus.value: Obama signed the stimulus bill into law
pol.stimulus.detail: The US year page's summary says this and similar legislation most notably gave Americans tax credits, and gives no dollar total for the package anywhere.

pol.blagojevich.label: Rod Blagojevich removed from office
pol.blagojevich.value: The Illinois governor became the first state governor impeached and removed in a quarter century
pol.blagojevich.detail: Pat Quinn was sworn in as the 41st governor of Illinois the same day.

pol.sotomayor.label: Sonia Sotomayor joins the Supreme Court
pol.sotomayor.value: She took the judicial oath as the third woman and the first Hispanic justice

pol.same_sex_marriage.label: Same-sex marriage legalised in three states
pol.same_sex_marriage.value: Iowa on April 3, Vermont on April 7 and New Hampshire on June 3
pol.same_sex_marriage.detail: The Iowa Supreme Court ruled unanimously that denying same-sex couples the right to marry was unconstitutional, which made Iowa the third state to allow it and the first in the midwest. Vermont's legislature overrode the governor's veto. John Lynch signed the New Hampshire bill, making it the sixth state.

world.recession.label: Global recession
world.recession.value: Gross world product shrank by 2.2 percent, its first contraction since World War II
world.recession.detail: The world year page cites the United Nations World Economic Situation and Prospects report, says unemployment rose and inflation fell across the world, and dates the start of a slow recovery to late in the year. The US year page says the American recession officially ended in June while job losses ran on through December at a smaller size.

world.h1n1.label: H1N1 swine flu pandemic
world.h1n1.value: The World Health Organization declared the outbreak a global pandemic on June 11
world.h1n1.detail: The WHO had already called the Mexican and American cases a public health emergency of international concern on April 24. The world year page's health section calls the pandemic the primary public health concern of the year and gives no case or death count.

world.hudson.label: US Airways Flight 1549 ditched in the Hudson River
world.hudson.value: All 155 people on board were rescued, in an accident that became known as the Miracle on the Hudson
world.hudson.detail: The US year page adds that the aircraft lost power in both engines shortly after taking off from LaGuardia and names the pilot as Chesley Sullenberger.

world.sri_lanka.label: Sri Lankan Civil War ended
world.sri_lanka.value: The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam were defeated militarily after more than 25 years of fighting
world.sri_lanka.detail: The world year page's conflicts section calls Eelam War IV, the war's final stage, the deadliest conflict of the year.

world.iran_protests.label: Protests across Iran
world.iran_protests.value: Mass demonstrations followed a disputed presidential election that returned Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, the largest in the country since the Iranian Revolution

world.earthquakes.label: Deadly earthquakes
value: L'Aquila, Italy, magnitude 6.3, April 6, 308 killed and more than 1,500 injured
Samoa, magnitude 8.1, September 29, at least 192 killed, with a tsunami that struck American Samoa and Tonga
Sumatra, Indonesia, magnitude 7.6, September 30, at least 1,115 killed
world.earthquakes.detail: The world year page's dated entries give 308 at L'Aquila and 1,115 on Sumatra, while its own environment section rounds the same two to approximately 300 and approximately 1,100. The dated figures are stated here and the rounded ones named rather than resolved.

world.lisbon_treaty.label: Treaty of Lisbon came into force
world.lisbon_treaty.value: It took effect on December 1, after the Czech Republic became the last European Union member state to sign on November 3
world.lisbon_treaty.detail: Ireland had approved the treaty in a second referendum on October 2. Herman Van Rompuy, then Prime Minister of Belgium, was designated the first permanent President of the European Council on November 3.

film.gross.label: Highest-grossing films, worldwide gross
value: Avatar, $2,743,577,587, 20th Century Fox
Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, $933,959,197, Warner Bros.
Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs, $886,686,817, 20th Century Fox
Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen, $836,303,693, Paramount
film.gross.detail: Worldwide gross rather than domestic, which is what the film page's table header states. Up, The Twilight Saga: New Moon, Sherlock Holmes, Angels & Demons and The Hangover fill out its top ten, running down from $735 million to $469 million. Avatar only reached theatres on December 18, and the film page says it broke many box office records and became the highest-grossing film of all time, so the figure printed against it is a cumulative worldwide run and not one year's takings. The Academy Awards page states a different basis for the same film, $596 million in domestic receipts by the nominations announcement the following February, when Up stood at $293 million and The Blind Side at $237.9 million.

film.best_picture.label: Best Picture
film.best_picture.value: The Hurt Locker, produced by Kathryn Bigelow, Mark Boal, Nicolas Chartier and Greg Shapiro
film.best_picture.detail: Awarded the following March at the 82nd Academy Awards, hosted by Alec Baldwin and Steve Martin at the Kodak Theatre in Hollywood. Bigelow became the first woman to win Best Director. The Hurt Locker took six awards and Avatar three, and the two had tied on nine nominations each. Sid Ganis announced on June 24 that the ceremony would carry ten Best Picture nominees instead of five, a count last used at the 16th ceremony in 1944. The other nominees were Avatar, The Blind Side, District 9, An Education, Inglourious Basterds, Precious, A Serious Man, Up and Up in the Air. Up became the second animated film nominated for Best Picture. Almost 42 million people in the United States watched the telecast.

film.acting_awards.label: Acting Oscars
value: Best Actor, Jeff Bridges, Crazy Heart
Best Actress, Sandra Bullock, The Blind Side
Best Supporting Actor, Christoph Waltz, Inglourious Basterds
Best Supporting Actress, Mo'Nique, Precious: Based on the Novel 'Push' by Sapphire
film.acting_awards.detail: Mark Boal won Best Original Screenplay for The Hurt Locker and Geoffrey Fletcher Best Adapted Screenplay for Precious, the first African American to win a screenwriting Oscar. Pete Docter took Best Animated Feature for Up, Michael Giacchino its score, and T Bone Burnett a share of Best Original Song for The Weary Kind from Crazy Heart. Meryl Streep's nomination for Julie and Julia was her thirteenth in the lead actress category, passing Katharine Hepburn.

film.world_cinema.label: Nominated for Best Foreign Language Film
value: The Secret in Their Eyes, Argentina, in Spanish, directed by Juan Jose Campanella, the winner
Ajami, Israel, in Arabic and Hebrew, directed by Scandar Copti and Yaron Shani
The Milk of Sorrow, Peru, in Spanish and Quechua, directed by Claudia Llosa
A Prophet, France, in French, Corsican and Arabic, directed by Jacques Audiard
The White Ribbon, Germany, in German, directed by Michael Haneke
film.world_cinema.detail: The White Ribbon took the Palme d'Or at the 62nd Cannes Film Festival and the Golden Globe in this category, A Prophet the BAFTA, and Broken Embraces the Critics' Choice award. The Milk of Sorrow won the Golden Bear at the 59th Berlin International Film Festival, where Asghar Farhadi took a Silver Bear for direction. Samuel Maoz's Lebanon won the Golden Lion at the 66th Venice International Film Festival, and Precious the People's Choice Award at the 34th Toronto International Film Festival.

film.releases.label: Releases
value: Up, May 29, Pixar's tenth feature film
The Princess and the Frog, December 11, Walt Disney Animation Studios' 49th feature film
Avatar, December 18, directed by James Cameron
Sherlock Holmes, December 25, directed by Guy Ritchie
film.releases.detail: The US year page dates the first three. The film page's events table adds that Sherlock Holmes took $25 million on Christmas Day and calls that a box office record for the day.

film.how_people_watched.label: How people watched
film.how_people_watched.value: In a theatre, and in 3-D more often than before. The film page's review of the year counts a dozen 3-D animated features and names DreamWorks Animation's Monsters vs. Aliens and Pixar's Up as the best of them.
film.how_people_watched.detail: None of the eleven cached pages mentions a disc format, a rental service, a subscription or any legal way to watch a film over the internet, so this fact claims nothing at all about home viewing.

tv.top_shows.label: Most-watched programs, season starting autumn 2009
value: American Idol, Tuesday, FOX, 13.7 rating
American Idol, Wednesday, FOX, 13.3
Dancing with the Stars, ABC, 12.6
NCIS, CBS, 11.5
Sunday Night Football, NBC, 11.3
tv.top_shows.detail: Nielsen reports by season, so this ranking covers the season that opened in the autumn and ran into the following spring. The Mentalist was sixth on 10.6, the Dancing with the Stars results show seventh on 9.9, NCIS: Los Angeles and Undercover Boss tied eighth on 9.8 and CSI: Crime Scene Investigation was tenth on 9.7.

tv.digital_switch.label: Analog television shut off in the United States
tv.digital_switch.value: Every remaining full-service NTSC station stopped broadcasting analog on June 12 and went digital only
tv.digital_switch.detail: Hawaii had switched all of its stations on January 15, the first state to finish. 368 stations went digital on the original February 17 deadline, and 53 at-risk stations kept analog signals under nightlight status for transition announcements and severe weather alerts. Obama signed the DTV Delay Act on February 11, which moved the cutoff to June 12. Game seven of the Stanley Cup final was the last broadcast to go out over analog.

tv.premieres.label: Programs that debuted
value: RuPaul's Drag Race, Logo, February 2
Parks and Recreation, NBC, April 9
Glee, Fox, May 19
Shark Tank, ABC, August 9
The Vampire Diaries, The CW, September 10
Archer and Community, FX and NBC, September 17
NCIS: Los Angeles and The Good Wife, CBS, September 22
Modern Family and Cougar Town, ABC, September 23
Jersey Shore, MTV, December 3
tv.premieres.detail: The television page's debut table gives each date and network. Bored to Death started on HBO on September 20. NBC put The Jay Leno Show into a weeknight ten o'clock slot on September 14, its first prime-time weeknight talk and variety show in years.

tv.audiences.label: Largest audiences
value: The Michael Jackson memorial service on July 7, broadcast live around the world to an estimated one billion people
The inauguration on January 20, carried by every major American broadcast and cable news network to a combined domestic audience of over 37.8 million
Packers against Vikings on ESPN's Monday Night Football on October 5, 15 million homes, the most-watched cable sports program to that point
tv.audiences.detail: The football game was Brett Favre's first against his former team, and the Vikings won it 30 to 23. The 81st Academy Awards, televised on February 22, drew 37 million in the United States for a ceremony honouring the previous year of film.

tv.emmys.label: 61st Primetime Emmy Awards
tv.emmys.value: Mad Men won Outstanding Drama Series and 30 Rock Outstanding Comedy Series
tv.emmys.detail: Hosted by Neil Patrick Harris and televised by CBS. The TV Guide report the television page cites is headlined on first Emmys for Kristin Chenoweth and Jon Cryer.

music.hot100_year_end.label: Year-end Hot 100 number one
music.hot100_year_end.value: Boom Boom Pow, The Black Eyed Peas
music.hot100_year_end.detail: Poker Face by Lady Gaga came second, Just Dance by Lady Gaga featuring Colby O'Donis third and I Gotta Feeling by The Black Eyed Peas fourth, so the two acts held the whole top four. Billboard counts the chart year from the first week of November to the final week of October and published this one on December 11. DJ Earworm cut the top twenty-five into a mashup video called Blame It On the Pop in late December.

music.best_selling_album.label: Best-selling album worldwide
music.best_selling_album.value: I Dreamed a Dream, Susan Boyle
music.best_selling_album.detail: 8.3 million copies in five weeks of release, on the IFPI ranking the music page reproduces. The E.N.D. by The Black Eyed Peas came second, This Is It by Michael Jackson third, Fearless by Taylor Swift fourth and The Fame by Lady Gaga fifth. Jackson also held eighth place with Thriller and ninth with Number Ones.

music.listening_format.label: How people listened
music.listening_format.value: Poker Face became the biggest-selling single of the year in the United Kingdom and the biggest-selling digital single there to that point
music.listening_format.detail: It returned to number one on the UK Singles Chart on March 22 and held the position three more weeks. The whole Beatles catalogue was reissued on September 9 as digital remasters, the first repackaging of it since 1987.

music.vmas.label: Kanye West interrupted Taylor Swift at the MTV Video Music Awards
music.vmas.value: He walked on stage during her acceptance speech for Best Female Video and said Beyonce had one of the greatest videos of all time
music.vmas.detail: Held at Radio City Music Hall in New York. Lady Gaga, Beyonce and Green Day each won three awards.

music.uk_christmas_number_one.label: UK Christmas number one
music.uk_christmas_number_one.value: Rage Against the Machine took it with Killing in the Name after a large Facebook campaign
music.uk_christmas_number_one.detail: The music page credits the campaign, and the BBC report it cites is headlined on the single beating the X Factor winner.

tech.bitcoin.label: Bitcoin network started
tech.bitcoin.value: The developer known as Satoshi Nakamoto mined the genesis block of the blockchain
tech.bitcoin.detail: The world year page and the science page both date it to January 3, both cite the same New Yorker profile, and neither says anything about who Nakamoto was.

tech.windows_7.label: Microsoft released Windows 7
tech.windows_7.value: Released to all computers and laptops, including an edition for cash machines
tech.windows_7.detail: The world year page dates the release to October 22. The US year page carries the same one-line entry twice, once under July 22 and once under October 22, with no wording to reconcile them, so the October date is stated here and the July entry named rather than resolved.

tech.internet_traffic.label: Michael Jackson's death overloaded the web
tech.internet_traffic.value: Reactions crippled several major websites and services, including a Twitter outage, and the number of people loading news pages pushed internet traffic to potentially unprecedented levels
tech.internet_traffic.detail: The US year page cites a CNN report from the following day and gives no traffic figure. Its own summary of the year says some websites crashed under the overflow.

tech.web_sites.label: WikiLeaks publications
value: 86 intercepted telephone recordings of politicians and businessmen from the Peru oil scandal, January 28
Kaupthing Bank's internal documents from before the Icelandic financial crisis, September 22
The membership list of the British National Party, October 20
tech.web_sites.detail: The Kaupthing papers showed suspiciously large loans made to the bank's own owners and debts being written off. The world year page carries all three and gives no figure for how many people read any of them.

tech.games.label: Video games
value: Minecraft, Mojang, May 17
The Sims 3, June 2
Batman: Arkham Asylum, Eidos Interactive, August 25
Uncharted 2: Among Thieves, Sony Computer Entertainment, October 13
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Activision, November 10
Left 4 Dead 2, Valve, November 17
Angry Birds, December 11, on iOS
tech.games.detail: Worldwide retail sales led with Wii Sports at 20,180,000 copies, then Wii Sports Resort at 13,580,000, Modern Warfare 2 at 11,860,000, New Super Mario Bros. Wii at 10,550,000 and Wii Fit Plus at 10,160,000. Uncharted 2 scored 96 out of 100 on Metacritic, the top of the games page's own list, and took Game of the Year at the Spike Video Game Awards on December 12. The 27th Golden Joystick Awards on October 30 gave theirs to the previous year's Fallout 3. The only new hardware was revisions: the Nintendo DSi reached North America on April 5, the PlayStation 3 Slim on September 1 and the PSP Go on October 1.

tech.spaceflight.label: Spaceflight
value: The Kepler space observatory launched on March 7 and began looking for exoplanets
Space Shuttle Atlantis flew the last servicing mission to the Hubble Space Telescope, May 11 to 24
The Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and LCROSS launched to the Moon on June 18, the first American lunar mission since Lunar Prospector in 1998
NASA announced on November 13 that LCROSS impact data showed a significant quantity of water in the Moon's Cabeus crater
MESSENGER made its final Mercury flyby on September 29
tech.spaceflight.detail: Iridium 33 and Kosmos 2251 collided over Siberia on February 10, the first accidental hypervelocity collision between two intact satellites in low Earth orbit, scattering debris in orbits 300 to 800 miles up. European astronomers announced 32 new exoplanets on October 20, and GJ 1214 b, found on December 16, was the first known exoplanet on which water could exist.

prices.gas.label: Average US gas price
prices.gas.detail: Unleaded regular, US city average, including taxes, annual average.

prices.min_wage.label: Federal minimum wage
prices.min_wage.detail: The basic rate for covered nonfarm workers, as in effect on December 31.

prices.unemployment.label: US unemployment rate
prices.unemployment.value: 7.8 percent in January, peaking at 10.0 percent in October
prices.unemployment.detail: The January figure was the highest since June 1992 and came in the month the US year page calls the worst of the recession, with nearly 800,000 jobs lost. The rate passed 9 percent in April for the first time since September 1983 and 9.5 percent in June, and the October peak was the highest since June 1983.

prices.dow.label: Dow Jones Industrial Average low
prices.dow.value: Bottomed at 6,547 on March 9 and then rose quickly
prices.dow.detail: Seventeen months to the day after its high of 14,164 on October 9, 2007. The US year page carries a citation-needed tag on this entry.

culture.mood.label: Mood
culture.mood.value: A president took office in January to a crowd that filled the Mall, and the job market shed workers every month of the year anyway. What people watched together was a pop star's funeral and a talent-show audition, both of them on the internet as much as on television.

culture.nobel_prizes.label: Nobel Prizes
value: Peace, Barack Obama
Literature, Herta Muller
Physics, Charles K. Kao, Willard Boyle and George E. Smith
Chemistry, Ada Yonath, Venkatraman Ramakrishnan and Thomas A. Steitz
Medicine, Elizabeth Blackburn, Carol W. Greider and Jack W. Szostak
Economics, Elinor Ostrom and Oliver E. Williamson
culture.nobel_prizes.detail: The world year page gives no dates. The US year page dates the Peace Prize announcement to October 9 and says the choice surprised many, Obama included. Mikhail Gromov took the Abel Prize.

culture.memes.label: Slender Man
culture.memes.value: A creepypasta character created by Eric Knudsen debuted in a forum on Something Awful
culture.memes.detail: The US year page's June 10 entry is the only mention anywhere in the cache and carries no citation.

culture.viral_video.label: Susan Boyle's audition
culture.viral_video.value: Her performance of I Dreamed a Dream on Britain's Got Talent was seen over 200 million times on YouTube and other video outlets
culture.viral_video.detail: The music page dates the broadcast to April 11 and gives the count as one combined figure across outlets rather than a YouTube total.

culture.balloon_boy.label: Balloon boy hoax
culture.balloon_boy.value: Parents claimed their young son had been carried away in a large balloon shaped like a spacecraft, setting off a wide rescue effort before admitting it was staged
culture.balloon_boy.detail: They were fined and given short jail sentences. The US year page gives no length for either.

sports.super_bowl.label: Super Bowl XLIII
sports.super_bowl.value: Pittsburgh Steelers 27, Arizona Cardinals 23, at Raymond James Stadium in front of 70,774
sports.super_bowl.detail: Santonio Holmes was named most valuable player. The US year page says the Steelers became the first NFL team to win six Super Bowls.

sports.world_series.label: World Series
sports.world_series.value: New York Yankees beat the Philadelphia Phillies four games to two, a 27th title
sports.world_series.detail: Hideki Matsui was named most valuable player. The US year page dates the clinching game to November 4.

sports.champions.label: Other championships
value: NBA Finals, Los Angeles Lakers over the Orlando Magic four games to one, with Kobe Bryant named most valuable player
Stanley Cup, Pittsburgh Penguins over the Detroit Red Wings on June 12, with Evgeni Malkin taking the Conn Smythe Trophy
NCAA men's basketball, North Carolina 89, Michigan State 72, at Ford Field in Detroit, a fifth title
NCAA women's basketball, Connecticut 76, Louisville 54, at the Scottrade Center in St. Louis, closing a 39 and 0 season
UEFA Champions League, Barcelona beat Manchester United 2 to 0 in Rome
World Baseball Classic, Japan beat South Korea 5 to 3 in extra innings at Dodger Stadium
AFL Grand Final, Geelong beat St Kilda by 12 points in Melbourne on September 26
sports.champions.detail: Shakhtar Donetsk won the UEFA Cup in extra time in Istanbul, Estudiantes the Copa Libertadores, Brazil the Confederations Cup over the United States 3 to 2 in Johannesburg and Mexico the Gold Cup over the United States 5 to 0. Panathinaikos took a fifth Euroleague title. Golf's men's majors went to Angel Cabrera at the Masters, Lucas Glover at the US Open, Stewart Cink at the Open Championship and Yang Yong-eun at the PGA Championship. Ireland won the Six Nations with a Grand Slam, and South Africa took the British and Irish Lions series 2 to 1.

sports.tennis.label: Tennis majors
value: Australian Open, Rafael Nadal over Roger Federer in five sets, and Serena Williams over Dinara Safina 6-0, 6-3
French Open, Federer over Robin Soderling 6-1, 7-6, 6-4, and Svetlana Kuznetsova over Safina
Wimbledon, Federer over Andy Roddick 16-14 in the fifth, and Serena Williams over Venus Williams
US Open, Juan Martin del Potro over Federer in five sets, and Kim Clijsters over Caroline Wozniacki
sports.tennis.detail: Spain beat the Czech Republic 5 to 0 in the Davis Cup and Italy beat the United States 4 to 0 in the Fed Cup.

sports.formula_one.label: Formula One
sports.formula_one.value: Jenson Button won his first world championship, driving for Brawn GP, at the Brazilian Grand Prix
sports.formula_one.detail: The world year page carries this and the sports page's own motorsport section is empty, so no other result for the season is stated here.

deaths.jackson.label: Michael Jackson
deaths.jackson.value: Died June 25, of an accidental overdose of propofol and benzodiazepines at his Los Angeles home. Born 1958
deaths.jackson.detail: Singer, songwriter, dancer and actor. He had announced the This Is It concert residency in London on March 5, and it was a fortnight from opening. A memorial service at Staples Center on July 7 was carried live around the world.

deaths.fawcett.label: Farrah Fawcett
deaths.fawcett.detail: American actress. The US year page puts her death on the same day as Michael Jackson's.

deaths.kennedy.label: Ted Kennedy
deaths.kennedy.detail: United States senator from Massachusetts from 1962.

deaths.mcnamara.label: Robert McNamara
deaths.mcnamara.detail: Business executive and the eighth United States Secretary of Defense.

notes: Research pass July 2026, from the cached wikitext under .sources/2009 plus one dedicated article pulled for the date check. Box office basis. bo.mjs reports GROSS from a header reading Rank, Title, Distributor, Worldwide gross, under a caption reading Highest-grossing films of 2009, so figures_basis is gross and film.gross names worldwide in both its label and its detail. film.mjs fails it: src/data/name_years.json allowlists Psychic Force 2012 but not the bare string. The title is a proper noun and belongs in the list, so it is reported here for an allowlist entry rather than written into any value or detail. Its distributor was Sony and the film page gives it $769,679,473 worldwide. Avatar's figure is flagged rather than picked: the film page prints $2,743,577,587 against a film that only opened on December 18, and the same page says it broke many box office records and became the highest-grossing film of all time, so that number is a cumulative worldwide run and not one calendar year's takings. The Academy Awards page states a different basis for the same film, $596 million domestic by the nominations announcement, and film.gross names both rather than reconciling them. Date check. An inauguration falls on January 20, and both cached year pages give January 20, so there is nothing to reconcile. First_inauguration_of_Barack_Obama was pulled as raw wikitext anyway and agrees; it is cited on pol.inauguration because the ceremony number, the West Front location, the flubbed oath, the January 21 re-administration in the Map Room and the record-attendance line all come from it and no cached page carries any of them. Source disagreements labelled rather than resolved. The world year page's dated entries give 308 dead at L'Aquila and 1,115 on Sumatra while its own environment section rounds the same two to approximately 300 and approximately 1,100, and world.earthquakes states the dated figures and names the rounded ones. The US year page carries the Windows 7 release twice, under July 22 and under October 22, with identical wording and no reconciliation; the world year page gives only October 22, which tech.windows_7 takes, naming the July entry. Nothing in this file reaches into the following year. The 82nd Academy Awards ceremony date, the Best Picture nominations announcement date, the 15th Critics' Choice and 67th Golden Globes and 63rd BAFTA dates, the 13th Interactive Achievement Awards, the 10th Game Developers Choice Awards, the 6th British Academy Games Awards, the Saturn ring-plane crossing's next occurrence, MESSENGER's orbital capture, the Rio de Janeiro Summer Games edition, the Celtic League's Italian expansion, the SANZAR Four Nations invitation, the Poplawski sentencing and the US year page's own claims about the Affordable Care Act, the Tea Party movement, the unemployment rate's later course and the next ten years are all out for that reason. film.best_picture and film.acting_awards say the following March rather than a date, which is the corpus convention. Host-city convention. The IOC awarded Rio de Janeiro the Summer Games on October 2 and Ireland approved the Lisbon Treaty in a second referendum the same day, and only the second is a fact here: naming the Games by their edition year is the forward-looking claim the anachronism check exists to catch, and the corpus convention is to give the city and the decision date instead. There was no room for a separate Olympic fact, so the award is out entirely rather than half-written. Dropped for lack of a source. Netflix, Hulu, iTunes, Spotify, Pandora, streaming of any kind, vinyl, DVD and Blu-ray appear in none of the eleven cached pages, which is why film.how_people_watched claims nothing about home viewing and music.listening_format rests on a single-territory sales claim. Usain Bolt and the Berlin World Championships records are absent from the cache, so there is no athletics fact. General Motors and Chrysler appear nowhere in the cache either, so the bankruptcy texture is Circuit City, the Chicago Cubs and CIT Group, which are the three the US year page actually carries.
